chunks: So they set out till they went on board a ship in which he made a hole, (and Moses said:) 'You have made a hole in the boat to drown its passengers? You have done a strange thing!'

key_terms.خَرَقَهَا: he made a hole in it

ai.seo_question: Why did Khidr damage the ship in Surah Al-Kahf?
ai.summary: In this verse, Prophet Moses (Musa) questions Khidr’s seemingly destructive act of damaging the ship, reflecting the initial tension between apparent surface meaning (zahir) and hidden divine wisdom (batin). Shia scholars often highlight this moment as the beginning of Khidr’s three lessons, illustrating that minor inconveniences can prevent greater calamities, a concept central to understanding divine decree (Qadr) and the unseen realities behind worldly events.
